item.title: Fujifilm Expands Magnetic Tape Production to Meet AI Data Storage Demand
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Fujifilm Expands Magnetic Tape Production Amid AI-Driven Data Storage Surge
Fujifilm announced plans to quintuple its magnetic tape production capacity by fiscal 2028, investing 10 billion yen ($63 million) to expand its Odawara plant. The project, spanning fiscal 2026-2028, will focus on 100TB cartridges for data storage, though annual output figures were not disclosed. The expansion responds to rising demand driven by generative AI adoption, which Fujifilm links to exponential data growth. The company emphasized magnetic tape’s role in cost-effective, secure backups for cloud providers and data centers, citing its air-gapped nature as a defense against ransomware. The Kanagawa Factory will be the project’s centerpiece, marking Fujifilm’s largest LTO tape facility expansion in over two decades. The company’s tape division, dating to the 1950s, introduced the LTO Ultrium10 in 2025, featuring hybrid magnetic particles. A 2026 IDC survey found 94.7% of organizations store more data post-AI adoption, with global data projected to reach 718 zettabytes by 2030. Fujifilm highlighted tape’s cost advantage at 1 cent per GB versus 3–3.5 cents for HDD storage. The move aligns with other Japanese investments in storage tech, including Kioxia’s ¥5 trillion semiconductor plan and Toshiba’s ¥60 billion hard-drive expansion. While magnetic tape remains niche, its use in enterprise data management is growing amid cybersecurity risks and storage demands.

item.title: North Korean Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion from Binance
item.description:
Source: PCMag, Digital Trends, Gizmodo, The Verge - Cybersecurities, TechCrunch, Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: North Korean Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion from Binance in Largest Crypto Heist
North Korean state-sponsored hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the largest cryptocurrency heist in history. Blockchain firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs attribute the attack to the group TraderTraitor, which exploited Binance’s internal systems using malicious code and the Ethereum upgrade EIP-7702. The hackers accessed Binance’s hot wallet, enabling rapid transfers across 10 blockchains within 20 minutes. Stolen assets included Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and stablecoins, totaling around $6.4 billion. The breach began with a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, allowing unauthorized withdrawals. Binance suspended withdrawals and froze $3 billion in company funds, with $6.34 billion reserved to cover losses. Hackers still hold $2.4 billion in assets, including 420,000 ETH and 18,000 Bitcoin, being laundered through automated transactions. TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the attack to TraderTraitor, also responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack and $387 million Bitget heist. Binance’s co-CEO Richard Teng called the breach a complex multi-point attack. The U.S. Secret Service and FBI are assisting in tracing funds, while experts warn of exchange vulnerabilities. Binance assures user funds are safe via its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

item.title: Strava integrates with Google Gemini for user insights
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Strava joins forces with Google Gemini—new insights are rolling out for users
Strava is integrating with Google Gemini to provide users with personalized insights from their fitness data. Subscribers can connect their accounts to view progress and receive analysis through Gemini's AI capabilities. The integration includes AI Performance Prediction, which requires at least 20 tracked activities to generate estimates for race times in 5K, 10K, and marathon distances. Users can ask Gemini to compare heart rate and speed across activities, break down racing performance per mile, and determine if weather or bodily factors affected performance. The feature is available in the U.S. for all Gemini plans. Strava previously introduced Athlete Intelligence, which analyzed non-GPS activities like treadmill runs and cycling power, and AI Performance Predictions, which rely on a user's activity history for accurate forecasts.

item.title: Anthropic Extension Backdoor Compromised, Affects 5,000 Developers
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
An official Anthropic Claude model extension for VS Code was backdoored, potentially compromising up to 5,000 developers’ machines. The malicious version 2.1.313, distributed through Cursor’s marketplace under Anthropic’s official account, included a persistent SSH backdoor via an attacker-controlled SSH key. The compromised extension, which auto-updates by default in Cursor, could grant attackers access to local files, source code, and developer tools across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Anthropic pushed a patched version 2.1.314 hours after the malicious release but has not publicly notified customers of the breach. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont and Phorian’s CTO Luke Roberts confirmed the supply-chain attack, noting the malicious code was posted to Anthropic’s official Cursor account. Cursor stated the backdoor enables reverse SSH tunnels, but neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attacker gained access to the account. The incident highlights risks in third-party distribution channels for developer tools.

item.title: Zest’s AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Zest’s new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
Zest, a restaurant discovery app, launched an AI-powered concierge that operates via text messages, enabling users to find and book reservations without opening a mobile app. The feature, similar to agents like Instinct or Poke, uses user history and friends’ data to make tailored recommendations. Founder Mario Gomez-Hall explained the AI starts from actual dining habits rather than requiring weeks of conversation. Zest links to users’ credit card data through Plaid to track dining patterns and suggest new places, focusing on food and drink transactions. The AI can check availability and book tables via OpenTable, Resy, and SevenRooms. Users can text the concierge at (212) 470-6067, join group chats for collective recommendations, and vote on options. TechCrunch tests found the AI effectively matched preferences with factors like time, party size, and location. Zest began testing the concierge last month but delayed the launch to add booking capabilities. The company aims to scale beyond its initial user base by monetizing bookings and future food ordering. Gomez-Hall noted the AI learns faster by starting from real dining data, offering value beyond just dinner.

item.title: Starbucks Tests AI-Driven Personalized Drive-Thru Menus
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru
Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol announced plans to use AI for personalized digital menus at drive-thru locations. During an earnings call, Niccol stated the company will explore technology to recognize customers as they arrive, display tailored menu options, and streamline payments. The initiative mirrors efforts by Taco Bell and McDonald’s, which use AI to adjust menu layouts and identify repeat customers. Starbucks will begin testing background AI models at drive-thrus starting in 2027 to improve order accuracy. The company also plans to integrate AI into its app for search and discovery, potentially enabling conversational ordering. Starbucks has already allowed ChatGPT for orders and introduced Green Dot Assist for employee support. Niccol emphasized the approach is "early," with testing, learning, and scaling to follow.

item.title: New Martian Meteorite Reveals Ancient Crust Insights
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
A team led by Yang Liu at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory has identified Teghaza 001, a Martian meteorite found in Mali’s Sahara Desert in 2022, as forming at least 4.1 billion years ago. This makes it the third known ancient Martian meteorite, joining Allan Hills 84001 and Black Beauty. Liu explained that most Martian meteorites on Earth are 2.4 billion years old or younger, suggesting a bias in the collection. The study highlights that large impacts are needed to eject rocks from Mars, but only certain materials survive. Teghaza 001 is a single, intact igneous rock, unlike Black Beauty, which is a mix of soil and fragments. Liu noted that the natural impact process filters out weaker rocks, leaving a biased sample. The discovery offers new insights into Mars’ ancient crust, as Teghaza 001 resembles some of Earth’s oldest rocks. The findings suggest current meteorite collections may not represent the planet’s full geological history.

item.title: Archaeologists Discover 2,700-Year-Old Bone Flute at Ancient Troy
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Archaeologists at Ancient Troy Unearth a 2,700-Year-Old Bone Flute. Odysseus Never Heard It
Archaeologists at Troy's archaeological site in modern-day Türkiye uncovered a 2,700-year-old bone flute fragment and a 4,500-year-old idol head. The idol, from the Early Bronze Age around 2500 BCE, was found beneath the FN Gate and may have had religious significance. The flute, dating to the 700s BCE, is the first identifiable musical instrument discovered at Troy, suggesting wind instruments were used in festivals and ceremonies. Reyhan Körpe, deputy director of the Troy Excavations, noted the findings highlight Troy's long history beyond Homer's Trojan War. The idol's context raises questions about sacred spaces at the gate, while the flute provides direct evidence of musical life in ancient Troy during the early first millennium BC. These discoveries underscore the city's continuous occupation and cultural evolution over millennia.

item.title: DoorDash Reports Minimal AI Agent Order Activity
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Ars Technica Original headline: DoorDash Reports Minimal AI Agent Order Activity Amid Industry Experimentation
DoorDash reported AI agents generated only 'several hundred' orders on its platform during the third quarter, according to CEO Tony Xu. The company, which processes nearly 1 billion annual orders, described AI agent use as a 'very low use case' compared to its daily delivery volume of 3 million. Xu emphasized the need to avoid overestimating or underestimating AI's potential, noting most users still rely on the app for orders. DoorDash has developed agents like a text-to-order tool, CLI agent, and chatbot Ask DoorDash, along with an MCP connector for corporate clients. However, broader consumer adoption remains limited, as the MCP is only available to a small number of early beta partners for lunch orders. Amazon has blocked AI agents, while Walmart uses them for customer acquisition. Xu suggested AI agents may eventually handle 'long consideration purchases' but are unlikely to replace the app for simple tasks like food ordering. The company's cautious approach reflects current limitations and industry uncertainty in AI-driven commerce.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: McAfee Helps Remove Personal Info From Data Brokers
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: How to Use McAfee to Get Your Personal Info Removed From Data Broker Sites
Data brokers collect personal information from public records, online activity, and third-party sources, then sell it to businesses. Users can manually opt out of data broker sites or use McAfee's Personal Data Cleanup tool to automate removal requests. McAfee+ Premium and higher plans scan data broker sites, identify listings, and handle removals. Manual removal requires visiting each site, searching for profiles, and submitting opt-out requests, which can take weeks. Automated tools like McAfee save time by scanning multiple sites and sending removal requests. While deletion requests may take 30-45 days, public records like property deeds or voter registrations remain unaffected. Experts recommend periodic checks to ensure data isn't reappearing. Privacy laws like California's CCPA grant consumers rights to delete data or opt out of sales, but data brokers often operate legally under state-specific rules.

item.title: PlotGTM Tool Helps Founders Estimate Go-To-Market Costs Before Spending
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: A new free tool shows founders what their go-to-market plan will really cost, before they spend a dime
PlotGTM launched a free go-to-market strategy calculator to help founders estimate costs before spending. The browser-based tool requires inputs like current revenue, revenue goals, campaign duration, lead volume, conversion rates, and pricing metrics. It calculates needed leads, customer acquisition costs, budget allocation across paid/earned media, required cash reserves, and payback timelines. The tool also adjusts for sales cycles, shifting funds toward content, PR, and email for longer cycles. A demo scenario for a $5 million company showed the tool identifying issues: the campaign would generate $1.7 million, falling short of a $3.5 million goal. Paid search costs $1,907 per customer, exceeding a safe ceiling of $972. The company needs $65,800 in cash upfront and a $34,800 monthly marketing team. PlotGTM emphasizes its assumptions are directional, citing research from Gartner, Forrester, and marketing experts. The tool aims to align stakeholders and test budget proposals before launch.

item.title: Lost Bose Earbud Found Using ChatGPT in Gravel Field
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Someone found their lost Bose bud in a field of gravel using ChatGPT, and it's genius
A Reddit user named Just-a-fungi893 found their lost Bose earbud in gravel using ChatGPT after 10 minutes of searching. They uploaded a photo of the area and asked the AI to locate the earbud, which identified its position. The AI's ability to detect small objects in large, uniform backgrounds like gravel is highlighted as a form of advanced pattern recognition. Other Reddit users shared similar experiences, such as finding a lost screw by asking ChatGPT to analyze a photo, though some cautioned about AI hallucinations, like a user who asked for book recommendations in a disorganized shelf and received fabricated titles. Alternative methods, like using a phone's flashlight or Find My features, were also mentioned. The incident underscores the growing utility of AI in tasks like object detection, though reliability varies by model and task.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Three Bash Variables Enhance Linux Terminal Navigation
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: These 3 simple bash variables add bookmarks and back buttons to your Linux terminal session
Three Bash features enhance Linux terminal navigation. CDPATH allows bookmarking directories by adding a colon-separated list of paths to ~/.bashrc. Typing 'cd website' navigates to a bookmarked folder if no local match exists. The leading dot in CDPATH ensures current directory precedence. OLDPWD stores the previous directory, enabling 'cd -' to toggle between last two locations. Pushd and popd manage a directory stack, allowing multiple directory jumps with 'dirs' to view the stack. These tools avoid plugins, provide tab completion with bash-completion, and handle common navigation patterns without exporting variables to prevent script conflicts.

item.title: NASA seeks commercial help to save Hubble from re-entry
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
Hubble Space Telescope faces re-entry in the early-to-mid-2030s after losing altitude since the last shuttle servicing in 2009. NASA issued a Request For Information asking commercial companies to propose methods for reboosting, servicing, or controlled disposal of the telescope. The RFI requires a reboost to at least 373 miles (600 km) by 2032, with contractors responsible for launch, spacecraft, operations, and crew if needed. NASA is not committing to funding a rescue mission but seeks bids on costs and feasibility. Current predictions suggest re-entry without intervention by 2033-2034, though solar activity could alter timelines. A reboost would extend Hubble’s operational life by at least 25 years. The deadline for responses is November 30.

item.title: 25% of U.S. Adults Lie to Doctors for Unneeded Antibiotics
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
A study led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah found 28% of U.S. adults lied to doctors to obtain unnecessary antibiotics. Of 1,371 survey respondents, 268 reported misrepresenting symptoms, with 141 exaggerating and 108 fabricating symptoms. Most lies involved falsely claiming viral infection symptoms like fever or sore throat, which antibiotics cannot treat. Despite the falsehoods, 77% of adult patients and 87% of caregivers received prescriptions. The research highlights widespread antibiotic misuse, with clinicians often complying with patients' dishonest claims. Thorpe’s team warns this undermines antimicrobial stewardship and public health efforts. A separate analysis of 263 caregivers found 27% misrepresented children’s symptoms for antibiotics.

item.title: AI Giants Back Standard to Let Publishers Opt Out of Scraping
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic, and Meta support a new standard allowing publishers to opt out of AI scraping. The shared 'policy token' signal, proposed by Anthropic's Kevin Kelley, will be added to websites' robots.txt files to control AI crawler access. Publishers can now apply AI training preferences across multiple companies instead of individually. Meta's Andy Stone supports the standard, though the company hasn't confirmed implementation. Microsoft will offer granular controls to block AI training or grounding, while Google and Microsoft plan to support the token next year. OpenAI will implement it in the coming months. The change addresses growing concerns about unauthorized scraping, with existing tools like RSL and Cloudflare offering limited protections. The IETF's Kelley emphasizes the importance of a unified signal for industry-wide adoption.

item.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Finale Focuses on Twin Avatars' Diverging Paths
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: The Season Finale of ‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Book One Got There in the End
Avatar: Seven Havens concludes its first book with a focus on twin avatars Nisha and Pavi navigating a world that resists their existence. The series diverges from past Avatar lore by reframing chakras as tools for personal growth rather than power-ups, emphasizing the twins' conflicting identities and struggles. Unlike predecessors, the finale avoids clear villains, instead portraying conflicts as consequences of flawed historical interpretations. Showrunner Sehaj Sethi designed the season without a defined antagonist, highlighting how past grievances shape present tensions. The twins' relationship evolves beyond a simplistic hero’s journey, with Nisha and Pavi diverging to define their own paths as avatars. While the series faces criticism for early inconsistencies, its finale marks a bold shift toward exploring legacy and self-discovery rather than retreading past narratives. The season’s strength lies in its complex characters and unresolved tensions, positioning the twins as the next generation grappling with the weight of history.

item.title: Akai's MPC Sample Key to Open-Source Software, Focus on Sample Playback
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Exclusive details about Akai’s MPC Sample Key
Akai teased its MPC Sample Key, planning to open-source its software for modding. Exclusive images reveal the device focuses on pitched sample playback rather than drum chopping. It lacks the 'chop' button from the MPC Sample, instead featuring pitch and mod wheels, octave range buttons, and controls for chord and arpeggiator modes. A dedicated looper is included, replacing Flex Beat effects with 'Swarm' functionality. The 25-key keyboard includes a built-in mic and speaker for all-in-one production. It supports MIDI and CV outs for modular synths. A correction notes the device has 25 keys, not 37.

item.title: AI Law Firm Bids for Disintegrating Weil Gotshal Assets
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: AI law firm Crosby bids on disintegrating, famed firm Weil Gotshal
AI-first law firm Crosby has submitted a bid to acquire assets from disintegrating firm Weil Gotshal & Manges, including its brand and internal data. The Information first reported the offer, which also involves hiring some of Weil’s 1,200 lawyers. Weil confirmed it is preparing to vote on dissolution, citing leadership changes, departures of top lawyers, and a failed merger with Willkie Farr & Gallagher. Crosby’s founders position their AI-driven model as the future of legal services, offering speed previously unattainable. The firm raised $85 million, including a $60 million Series B round in March 2025. While AI’s role in Weil’s decline isn’t specified, the bid highlights its potential to reshape the legal industry. Terms of the acquisition remain undisclosed, and success is uncertain. If Crosby wins, Weil’s legacy could be reimagined through AI integration.

item.title: tvOS 27.2 adds screen saver shuffle, FaceTime upgrades, and Find My support
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: New tvOS 27.2 features to try for an upgraded Apple TV experience
Apple released tvOS 27.2 with new features for Apple TV, including enhanced screen savers and FaceTime improvements. The update adds a 'Shuffle' option for screen savers, cycling through Aerials, Memories, Portraits, and Snoopy, and allows iPhone users to select specific photos without sharing their entire library. FaceTime now supports third-party sign language interpreters and live captioning via Continuity Camera. The new Apple TV 4K remote includes Find My support and a speaker, appearing in the Find My app. Profile support for the Apple TV app syncs across iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV, with new profile options. A black-and-white Apple Music icon matches iOS 27.2's design. The update is free for Apple TV 4K models from 2021 onward, but surround sound features require the newer A19 chip model. Updates are available via Settings > System > Software Update.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Samsung phone users can protect privacy with five settings when lending devices
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Change these 5 Samsung settings before letting someone borrow your phone
Samsung phone users can protect privacy with five settings when lending devices. Secure Folder locks private photos in a password-protected space. Notification content is hidden from the lock screen to prevent sensitive messages from being seen. App pinning restricts access to only the Phone app, preventing unauthorized app openings. Privacy Alerts flag apps with unusual permission requests, allowing users to revoke unnecessary access. Privacy Display limits side-angle viewing to prevent accidental screen exposure. These settings help maintain control over personal data when sharing devices, ensuring borrowed phones don't compromise privacy. The configurations require minimal setup but provide significant protection against unintended data exposure.

item.title: Sony Launches Compact 3D Display for Anime Avatars
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Sony has shrunk its glasses-free 3D technology into a tiny screen, and it can bring anime characters to life on your desk
Sony has released the ELF-MN1, a 6-inch glasses-free 3D display that projects 3D characters and avatars without requiring special glasses or a headset. The device uses eye-tracking sensors to adjust the image in real time, creating a 3D effect by having each eye view a slightly different perspective. It operates within a 12 to 31-inch range and requires a recent smartphone or USB-C-enabled PC with DisplayPort Alt Mode support. The display features 403 pixels per inch resolution and reduces crosstalk artifacts. It connects via USB-C and runs Gugenka’s HoloModel service, offering digital anime figures. Priced around 54,000 yen ($340), the ELF-MN1 launches in Japan on December 11, 2026, with demo units available at Sony Stores in Ginza and Nagoya starting November 20. The device aims to bring 3D anime characters to desks, though only one viewer can experience the full 3D effect at a time.

item.title: AO3 Outage Continues as Security Incident Investigation Ongoing
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Popular Fan Fiction Site AO3 Could Be Offline for a Month Following ‘Security Incident’
Archive of Our Own (AO3) remains offline after a security incident caused a prolonged outage. The nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) initially attributed the outage to maintenance but later confirmed it was due to a security breach. OTW warned the site could be offline for up to four weeks, potentially in a degraded state with limited features. No user content was deleted, but the organization could not confirm if user data was compromised. AO3 hosts over 18 million fanworks and 11 million users. Fans expressed frustration on social media, with some questioning their trust in the site. The incident follows other recent cybersecurity breaches, including PHP vulnerabilities and a leaked DHS employee database. OTW continues investigating the security incident and will provide updates as more information becomes available.

item.title: Battery-Powered Water Taxi Debuts for Commuting on Potomac River
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Can This Battery-Powered Water Taxi Jumpstart a Potomac River Ferry System?
Vessev's VS-9 battery-powered water taxi debuted on the Potomac River, showcasing its electric propulsion system and hydrofoil design. Unlike competitors like Candela and Arc Boats, Vessev focused on a 10-passenger model for commuting rather than luxury craft. CEO Eric Laakmann highlighted the simplicity and reliability of the powertrain, comparing it to a tractor. The VS-9 achieves 25 knots (29mph) with hydrofoil struts, offering a smooth ride and minimal wake, crucial for the Potomac's no-wake zones. The boat has a 40-nautical-mile range with a full load and can charge in an hour via DC fast chargers. A September study suggested electric hydrofoils could enable faster, more frequent ferry service if allowed to bypass no-wake restrictions. The VS-9's large glass windows provide scenic views but lack robust air conditioning in early models. Laakmann proposed marina-based battery charging solutions, likening them to AirPods cases. Vessev did not disclose pricing details.

item.title: GM to pay $22.0 million after sharing customer data with insurers
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
General Motors agreed to pay $220 million after sharing customer data from its Smart Driver system with brokers, who sold it to insurance companies. The data, used to monitor teen drivers or track adult behavior, led to higher insurance rates for some drivers who had not consented to the sharing. In 2023, GM and OnStar settled with the FTC, banning data sharing for five years and discontinuing Smart Driver. Now, GM has reached a settlement with 35 states and the District of Columbia after their attorneys general sued the company. The agreement requires a third party to assess GM’s compliance with its new privacy program. GM stated its commitment to transparency, noting connected vehicle data enables 'safer, more helpful and personalized experiences' while ensuring customer control over shared information.

item.title: Apple considers OLED upgrade for iMac, but delays expected
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple’s next big OLED upgrade could appear on the iMac
Apple's new iMac features the M6 chip and improved connectivity but lacks major design changes. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple is considering an OLED screen upgrade for the iMac, though it may take years to materialize. An OLED iMac would position the desktop as a luxury product, as few mainstream all-in-one computers offer such screens at its price range. Apple has increasingly adopted OLED displays across devices like iPhones, Apple Watches, iPads, and MacBooks. The iMac's design has remained largely unchanged since its 2021 M1 refresh, with the 2026 model continuing the same approach. Gurman suggests the OLED upgrade might target the long-rumored 27-inch iMac or a revived iMac Pro. The shift to OLED aligns with Apple's trend of integrating the technology into its product lineup, though the iMac's current design has not seen significant evolution.

item.title: Salesforce Acquires Rune Technologies for $375M in Defense Tech Deal
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune
Salesforce has agreed to acquire Rune Technologies, a defense tech startup developing AI software for U.S. military logistics, for $375 million in cash and stock. The deal expands Salesforce’s defense sector efforts through its Missionforce unit, which saw 80% year-over-year revenue growth since launching last year. Missionforce’s growth is partly driven by a $5.6 billion, 10-year contract with the U.S. Army. By integrating Rune’s frontline logistics data, Missionforce aims to support battlefield operations beyond administrative planning. Rune, founded in 2024, raised $30 million in funding, including from Andreessen Horowitz and IQT, and was last valued at $127 million. Salesforce has pursued multiple acquisitions this year, including $3.6 billion for Fin, $1.2 billion for Qualified, and a pending deal for Listen Labs. Salesforce declined to comment on the acquisition.

item.title: Intel Launches Nova Lake CPUs to Challenge AMD in High-End Desktop Market
item.description:
Source: PCMag, Gizmodo Original headline: Intel Set to Launch Nova Lake CPUs to Compete with AMD in High-End Desktop Market
Intel announced the Nova Lake CPU family to challenge AMD in the high-end desktop market. The new chips will use Intel’s 18A-P manufacturing process, aiming to regain market share from AMD’s Ryzen X3D processors, which hold 34.9% of the desktop CPU market. Intel’s current flagship, the Core Ultra 9 285K, has faced criticism for limited gaming performance compared to AMD’s Ryzen 9 9950X3D. The Nova Lake lineup is expected to deliver improved gaming performance, with CFO David Zinsner stating the company aims to gain market share. However, Intel acknowledged a 20% decline in PC shipments during Q3 due to memory shortages. The flagship Nova Lake chip may feature up to 52 CPU cores, with details revealed at CES in January. Intel is also integrating advanced memory technologies like bLLC to enhance real-time graphics. While leakers suggest potential gaming performance boosts of 8-20%, Intel has not confirmed these figures. CEO Lip-Bu Tan expressed confidence the lineup will surpass its predecessor, Panther Lake, in design wins. Despite financial challenges, Intel’s focus on high-end desktop chips reflects the growing influence of PC gamers on the market.

item.title: Google Enables Friends to Appear Together in Gemini Avatars
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google makes Gemini’s AI avatars social, so friends can now appear in each other’s content
Google is updating Gemini’s AI avatars to allow users to share their digital likeness with friends, enabling them to appear together in AI-generated images and videos. Users can create personal avatars by recording their face and voice via the Gemini website, following setup instructions that include recording in a well-lit environment without facial obstructions. Once created, avatars can be tagged in prompts using a username handle, and shared with others via Gmail invitations. Recipients can accept or decline access, and users retain control over permissions. The feature requires a Google account and is restricted to users aged 18 or older. It currently supports English and is unavailable in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. Google emphasizes that avatars are based on recorded appearances and voices for accurate recreation in generated content.

item.title: Apple launches Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
Apple will introduce Apple Intelligence features in China via iOS 27.3, announced on its Chinese newsroom website. The iOS 27.3 beta launches November 4, with a full release planned for December. Features include notification summaries, real-time translation, rewriting and proofreading tools, visual intelligence, and photo editing. Alibaba’s Qwen chatbot integration is added for some experiences, similar to iOS’s ChatGPT integration. Apple trained a dedicated large language model for China, approved by regulators in July. The launch marks the first phase of Apple Intelligence in the region, excluding the new Siri AI. The features aim to enhance user experience with AI-driven tools tailored to Chinese markets.

item.title: Audio-Technica Launches Wireless Headset for Streamers
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Audio-Technica’s new wireless StreamSet headset promises studio sound without the cables
Audio-Technica launched the ATH-M50xSTS-WL wireless headset, combining studio-grade audio from its ATH-M50x monitors with microphone tech from its 20 Series mics. The headset uses a 2.4 GHz radio link via USB dongle for low-latency, interference-resistant connectivity within 33 feet. It features a cardioid condenser microphone with adaptive noise reduction and sidetone for voice clarity. Two earpad options balance sound quality and comfort, with 24 hours of battery life and wired fallback. Priced at $299, it targets streamers and gamers prioritizing audio fidelity. Available since October 28, 2026, the device emphasizes studio sound without cables.

item.title: Cisco's 27-Year-Old Engineer to Refactor 98% of Legacy Code in 24 Months
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Cisco gives 27-year-old engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite 98% of the company's legacy code in 24 months
Cisco's president Jeetu Patel has tasked 27-year-old engineer Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy with rewriting 98% of the company's legacy code within 24 months. Krishnamurthy, a former startup founder acquired by Cisco in 2023, was previously in a low-level role. Patel gave him unlimited AI tokens to accelerate the project, citing his ability to refactor code with just two people. Patel argues that traditional corporate structures stifle innovation and seeks to hire more young professionals who can challenge the status quo. He acknowledges potential friction between Gen Z employees and older staff but believes tension fosters creativity. Patel emphasizes combining experienced operators with AI-native hires to drive results, stating 'either of these groups by themselves aren't nearly as potent as when all three work together.'

item.title: Thousands of “ghost students” use AI to steal millions in student loans, DOJ says
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
The US Department of Justice charged five individuals in a crackdown on 'ghost students'—fraudsters using AI to steal identities and siphon student loans. The DOJ seized over $750,000 in cryptocurrency from a network linked to Kenyan nationals after data analysis flagged fraud. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald credited Trump-era fraud-detection measures for the arrests, calling it 'the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.' He warned fraudsters that enforcement is ongoing, stating, 'Whether you are in Nebraska, New Jersey, Virginia, or Nairobi, we will pursue you.' The scheme involves purchasing personal data of Americans, filing fake FAFSA applications, and funneling aid through bank accounts controlled by fraudsters. Dozens of Americans have acted as money mules, the DOJ said. FBI and Education officials joined McDonald to detail how the fraud operates, emphasizing the use of stolen identities to exploit student aid programs.

item.title: Nothing OS 5.0 Update Rolls Out for Phone 3a and 4a Series
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Phone 3a, Phone 4a series—it's your turn to receive Nothing OS 5.0 (Android 17)
Nothing released OS 5.0 (Android 17) for Phone 3a and 4a series on October 30, with a staggered rollout. The update includes camera enhancements for Phone 3a, such as dual-view video, filters, tuning effects, and seven adjustable presets. Phone 4a gains simultaneous front/rear camera recording with dual-view video and a refreshed camera UI. Essential Voice on 4a improves transcription speed. The Phone 3 received its OS 5.0 update in mid-October, featuring customization options, Essential AI tools, a Glyph Interface app, and the Geist typeface. Smart Collections on Phone 3 now automatically organize content. Both 3a and 4a series received UI refinements for camera controls and animations. Updates for Phone 4a Pro follow later in the Android 17 rollout.

item.title: Roman Scotland Man's Face Reconstructed from Skeleton
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: A Broken Nose, a Damaged Arm, and a Gruesome Grave. This Man From Roman Scotland Now Has a Face
National Museums Scotland reconstructed the face of a man who lived in Roman Scotland around 140-165 CE. His skeleton showed injuries to his nose and right arm, likely from trauma, and signs of septic arthritis. The man was buried in a grave with four decapitated individuals, though his own decapitation status is unclear. Scientists used osteoarchaeology, DNA, and isotopic analysis to determine he originated from southern Britain and traveled to Scotland. His reconstructed face, created by Chris Rynn, depicts a man in his early 50s who likely struggled with daily tasks due to his injuries. The burial site at Inveresk is the first Scottish example of post-mortem decapitation, a practice possibly linked to ritual or belief systems. The museum will display the skeleton and reconstruction in an exhibition starting November 14. Curator Fraser Hunter noted the family would have recognized the likeness, highlighting the man’s personal history through scientific techniques.

item.title: Intel's Stock Plunge Sparks Semiconductor Market Turmoil
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Latest from Tom's Hardware
Intel's stock fell 30% on Friday, marking its worst single-day decline, wiping out $150 billion in market value. The drop followed a warning that fourth-quarter revenue would miss analyst expectations, projected between $15B-$16B versus $17B forecasts. The semiconductor sector index (SOX) dropped 9.14%, with server makers like Dell, HPE, and Oracle also losing value. Intel's government stake, purchased in 2025, lost $12 billion but remains profitable. The company's client computing group reported $8.1B revenue in Q3 2026, down 5% YoY and 14% in shipments. Intel warned of a 10% PC market shrinkage in 2027 due to supply constraints. Its data center business grew 78% YoY, but Arizona fab limitations hinder demand. The next major plant is not expected until 2028. Intel's stock fluctuated between $673.43B and $338.91B. NVIDIA, which holds an Intel stake, also saw a $270B market cap decline. The broader semiconductor market lost $1 trillion in value, reflecting widespread sector challenges.

item.title: Intel leaker reveals Moon Lake chip as a likely replacement for N-series SoCs
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware
Intel leaker Jaykihn revealed base specs for Moon Lake, a chip expected to replace N-series SoCs. The design features four low-power-efficiency (LP-E) cores and no performance cores, with TDP ranging from 6 W to 15 W. It mirrors Wildcat Lake's layout, placing efficiency cores in their own island. The chip targets laptops and mini-PCs priced between $300 and $500, though exact costs vary with RAM and storage. Moon Lake is slated for 2028, with NAND and DDR supply timelines uncertain. Clock speeds remain unspecified, though newer Intel chips like Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake maintain similar speeds to their predecessors. While Moon Lake retains the 4-LPE core count and 6 W TDP of N-series designs, its new architecture may offer improved battery life compared to older models.

item.title: Apple Adds Remote Tracking in iOS 27.2 Update
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple has finally made it easier to find your lost TV remote, and it’s about time
Apple added remote tracking in iOS 27.2, allowing Find My app to locate Apple TV 4K remotes. Previously, users had to use Control Center for this feature, which many likely overlooked. The update integrates remote tracking into the Find My app used for AirPods, Apple Watch, and MacBook, improving accessibility. Fourth-generation Siri Remotes support Precision Finding, guiding users with directional cues and a built-in speaker. These remotes come with the new Apple TV 4K and cost $59. Precision Finding requires an iPhone 17 or newer, limiting older devices to basic tracking. The update aims to streamline lost remote recovery without requiring new purchases. Users with older iPhones will only get standard Find My tracking without advanced features.

item.title: Subvocal’s smart glasses convert silent speech to text
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Subvocal’s glasses promise to let you talk to your computer in complete silence
Subvocal’s smart glasses convert silent mouth movements into text at over 200 words per minute. The device uses radar signals to detect subtle facial muscle movements when users silently form words, then interprets those changes via AI to generate text. No cameras are used, and users must deliberately mouth words. The startup claims the glasses can enable private conversations across crowded spaces and allow tasks like messaging, note-taking, and interacting with AI assistants. Subvocal has raised $1.3 million from Y Combinator and Afore Capital, with early-bird pricing at $499 requiring a $199 refundable deposit. Prescription lenses will cost extra, and shipping is expected to begin in early 2027. The technology remains unverified, and challenges like handling accents or unfamiliar words are yet to be addressed.

item.title: AI-designed virus tested in human for antibiotic-resistant infection
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: A human subject has been injected with an AI-designed virus aiming to kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria, so let's see how that turns out
Radical Numerics, a San Francisco AI lab, administered its AI-designed bacteriophage Omnii-1 to a patient with a drug-resistant E. coli infection in October 2026. The treatment, part of a compassionate-use pathway authorized by the FDA, marks the first time an AI-generated organism was used in a human as medicine. The phage was engineered by modifying the T7 virus's tail fiber to target specific bacterial receptors. While the company claims the treatment eliminated the patient's infection in vitro, no clinical results, peer review, or patient details have been disclosed. The company self-published technical findings showing 69.9% viability in designed variants, surpassing random controls. Experts remain cautious, noting the lack of published data and the need for peer review. The approach could revolutionize phage therapy by accelerating design, but raises concerns about AI-driven biological design's dual-use potential. Radical Numerics aims to commercialize the technology, which could address growing antimicrobial resistance linked to 4.7 million deaths in 2021 globally.

item.title: AI Vendors Grapple with Data-Sharing Rules as HubSpot Reverses Plan
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business
AI vendors face data-sharing dilemmas similar to 1990s data cooperatives, which operated on clear give-to-get terms. Modern AI platforms, however, lack such rules, allowing customer data to enrich shared models without explicit consent. HubSpot encountered backlash when it planned to pool enrichment data across accounts by default, prompting a reversal to opt-in terms. Sales teams feared their cleaned data would benefit competitors without compensation. McKinsey's 2026 survey found only 30% of organizations have mature AI governance. Vendors struggle to define exit terms, as removing data from trained models is technically impossible. Contracts must now clarify what persists after cancellation. Opt-in consent addresses part of the issue but lacks guarantees for returns. Vendors must transparently explain data economics in product and contract terms to avoid disputes. Buyers are pushing for clarity on data usage, mirroring past demands for security certifications.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: SALES: Sintra AI's AI Employees Help Small Businesses Grow
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: What Do AI Employees Actually Do? How Sintra AI Helps Small Businesses Grow
Sintra AI offers 12 AI Employees to automate business tasks for small businesses. These AI roles handle social media management, SEO, content creation, email automation, and customer support. Soshie, the AI Social Media Manager, streamlines content planning, generation, and scheduling, boosting website engagement by 109% for a solo legal services operator. Seomi, the AI SEO Specialist, increases monthly recurring revenue by $3,000 and generates 15 additional leads monthly for the same business. Sintra AI consolidates multiple tools into a single platform, reducing costs and administrative overhead. The company raised $17M in June 2025. AI Employees are designed to assist, not replace, human workers, enabling small business owners to focus on strategic tasks. Roles include Penn (copywriting), Commet (website building), Emmie (email), Cassie (customer support), and others. Businesses can customize their AI team based on needs, scaling as required.

item.title: Dartmouth Provost Resigns After AI Use Disclosure Violation
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Dartmouth's provost warned us about AI cheating—but his own AI use cost him his job
Dartmouth College provost Santiago Schnell resigned after an advisory committee found he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and a Washington Post op-ed, despite required disclosures. The committee accessed his Claude enterprise account, revealing he used the LLM to revise papers, debug code, and generate figures. Schnell told Semafor he used chatbots to refine arguments and check grammar, describing AI as an editorial aid. He claimed he did not disclose AI use because he did not understand it required disclosure. The committee criticized his insufficient cooperation, noting he did not provide personal LLM logs or meet with investigators. Schnell’s actions contradict his earlier warnings about AI cheating in academia.

item.title: Cannabis Users Most Likely to Call Psychedelic Hotline Mid-Trip
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: The Callers Most Likely to Phone a Psychedelic Hotline Mid-Trip Weren’t on Psychedelics
The Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line, active from 2021 to 2026, compiled 25,419 anonymized calls into a database for psychedelic epidemiology. Researchers found that while 60% of callers discussed psilocybin, cannabis users were most likely to seek help mid-trip. Nearly half (47%) of cannabis callers experienced panic or concern over their use, with 70% seeking active-trip support compared to 25% for integration. MDMA and ketamine callers were more likely to seek post-trip integration (66% and 59%, respectively). Researchers noted cannabis-related distress calls (2,004 total) highlight real psychological risks, though higher call volumes may reflect broader user populations rather than higher risk. The study, published in Science Advances by Joshua White and Mickael Eskinazi, argues cannabis’s legal status and widespread use demand better crisis support frameworks. The database aims to inform policymakers on distress patterns and support needs across psychoactive substances.

item.title: Rivian tests autonomy ambitions with 2026 driverless rollout
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Rivian’s autonomy gamble faces its first real test
Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe prioritized autonomous vehicle ambitions over production updates during an earnings call. The company plans to launch a point-to-point hands-free driving feature for employees in 2026 and customers in 2027, followed by robotaxi partnerships with Uber in 2028. Scaringe called the system a "wonderful" experience for his daily commute, emphasizing its potential to drive demand. However, Rivian faces financial risks from costly custom chips, lidar sensors, and AI infrastructure, which could eat into profits from scaling the R2 SUV. VP Derek Mulvey called autonomy a "primary product differentiator" and market share driver. Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) has a 75% take rate in North America, while Rivian reported $605 million in software revenue for Q3 2026, up 45% year-over-year. Challenges include edge cases, urban driving complexities, and legal risks from potential crashes. Rivian must balance launching the R2 at scale with becoming a full-stack autonomy player, a high-stakes gamble against Tesla and Waymo.
